handoff.purpose: Define import scanning helpers, resolution, entry-point discovery, and start of analyse function.

symbols.name: _shim_body
symbols.note: Checks if a module body is a shim (only imports, assigns, try/if with pass/imports). Returns bool.

symbols.name: _scan
symbols.note: Parses text, splits imports, collects literals, dispatch chains, main guard, and dynamic imports. Returns _Src.

symbols.name: _branch_payload
symbols.note: Extracts import records and names from an if branch body, excluding orelse.

symbols.name: _iter_funcs
symbols.note: Generator yielding (name, ast node) for all functions and methods recursively.

symbols.name: _collect_funcs
symbols.note: Populates src.func_records, func_names, func_loops, func_calls by walking functions.

symbols.name: _is_forever
symbols.note: Returns True if a while/for loop is infinite (constant True test).

symbols.name: _scan_dynamic
symbols.note: Scans for importlib/__import__ calls; records literals as dyn_targets, others as dynamic.

symbols.name: _resolve
symbols.note: Resolves import records to relative paths, excluding self.

symbols.name: _package_parents
symbols.note: Returns parent __init__.py paths for a given relative path.

symbols.name: _SECTION_RE
symbols.note: Regex to match any section header.

symbols.name: _SCRIPT_LINE_RE
symbols.note: Regex to parse script entry lines.

symbols.name: _console_scripts
symbols.note: Parses pyproject.toml for console_scripts entries without tomllib.

symbols.name: _func_closure
symbols.note: Returns transitive callees of a function within the same module.

symbols.name: analyse
symbols.note: Main entry: scans repo, resolves imports, builds graph (partial).

claims.text: ``orelse`` is deliberately excluded: for an elif chain the orelse IS the next branch, and folding it in would credit every subcommand with every later subcommand's imports.
claims.why: The function explicitly operates on node.body only, not orelse, matching the claim.

claims.text: A literal argument is a REAL edge and is treated as one. A non-literal one is a hole in the static picture; it is recorded so the report can say a module is ``unknown`` instead of accusing it of being an island.
claims.why: Code adds literal strings to dyn_targets, non-literals to dynamic set.

claims.text: ``__init__.py`` files Python imports as a side effect of importing this module. These edges are real at runtime -- omitting them would report a package's ``__init__`` as an island whenever nothing imports it by name.
claims.why: Function computes parent __init__.py paths from rel, as described.

claims.text: Hand-parsed because ``tomllib`` landed in 3.11 and this package targets 3.10 with zero runtime dependencies.
claims.why: Code uses regex parsing, not tomllib, consistent with claim.

claims.text: Every function of this module transitively called from ``start``.
claims.why: Function performs BFS over func_calls to collect transitive callees.

claims.text: ``index`` is an optional structcore index dict. Any edge it has that this walk does not is REPORTED in ``index_extra_edges`` and is NOT added to the graph: structcore resolves imports without branch context, so unioning its edges back in re-admitted exactly the ``if False:`` and swallowed-``ImportError`` imports this engine refuses on purpose, and printed the target ``reachable``. A disagreement between the two engines is a finding, not a discovery, and a finding may not quietly promote a module.
claims.why: The docstring describes behaviour involving index_extra_edges and comparison with structcore; this chunk does not contain that logic (analyse is incomplete).

claims.text: Resolved exactly like real ones, then kept OUT of ``edges``. They exist only to answer "why is this module here at all", so an unreached module somebody clearly intended to load is ``unknown`` rather than an island.
claims.why: The comment describes weak edge handling, but the code for resolution and exclusion from edges is not present in this chunk (analyse incomplete).

observations.what: _shim_body returns False on any non-import/assign/try/if statement; assigns must be simple (single Name target, value is Name/List/Tuple/Attribute). Try/If bodies must consist only of imports/pass.
_scan collects string literals up to 400 chars into src.literals.
_scan_dynamic only checks first argument of call; if call has no args, it records as dynamic (non-literal).
analyse function incomplete; ends after defining weak_edges list.
_console_scripts returns sorted list; handles missing file and OSError.
_func_closure uses BFS over func_calls; skips if start not in func_records.
Collisions in dotted names cause both to be removed from rel_by_dotted.
